/v/QuestForZen is a new sub dedicated to helping coach people that have recently discovered the peace that comes with the study and application of Zen Philosophy. I myself am new to the Zen scene and thought that it would be nice to have a place to go where I can document and collaborate with other people seeking peace.

There is Taoism and several schools of Buddhism mixed with a plethora of other spiritual movements. I have read of people that use yoga as a form of meditation. There are terms like Mind, Tao, and everything in between. I set this suverse up not just as a means to collaborate, but for exposure. There are so many styles and philosophies. I would love to meet them all!

The sub has been around for about a day, and I am still reacquainting myself with CSS and feeling out the visual changes. Feel free to drop in and discuss!

What Al-Bassam and Tynan theorized was that the government may have targeted parts of the Apple devices that it “doesn’t trust”: pieces that can retain bits of electronic information even after the hard drive is obliterated.

According to the public documents from other members of Five Eyes, it is incredibly difficult to completely sanitize a device of all its content.

Linux works best with FAT file systems

Almost everything can read FAT file systems, because they are quite simple. For running Linux from it, don't use FAT. USE ext4 or btrfs or XFS.
I wouldn't suggest using Btrfs yet. Ext4 is the best choice. It's not the default in pretty much every distro for nothing.
You shouldn't use btrfs yet on multiple disks like mdraid or raidz, but on a single one it is stable according to it's devs. It might not be present in all the tools yet though.

I still don't trust it. I mean, if you know what you're getting into then cool, but don't recommend it to newbies. Until it's been default on a tier-1 distro for multiple releases, I wouldn't touch it.

you can use a live CD and us gparted to mess with your partition (if you have a lot of free space) and then you should be able to duel boot without having to backup anything. I mean backup files you would normally, but you don't have too. And as @stavon said, use ext4 or btrfs, or xfs.
